body_markdown:
# Introduction

The question “Tell me about yourself” is common in interviews. Your answer should be relevant to the job and usually take about 45 to 90 seconds. You do not need to tell your entire life story.

## 1. Use a simple structure

1. Greeting and your name.
2. Your current role or education.
3. Relevant experience or skills.
4. One strength connected to the job.
5. Why you are interested in the opportunity.

## 2. Sample answer for an experienced candidate

“Good morning. My name is Rahul. I have experience in customer support and office coordination. In my previous role, I handled customer queries, maintained records and worked with different teams. I am organised, responsible and willing to learn. I am interested in this position because it matches my experience and gives me an opportunity to contribute to the team. Thank you.”

This is a sample. Replace the details with your real experience and skills.

## 3. Sample answer for a fresher

“Good morning. My name is Priya. I have recently completed my graduation. I am interested in starting my career in administration. I can communicate clearly, use basic computer applications and work well with a team. I am eager to learn and take responsibility. Thank you for this opportunity.”

## 4. Useful phrases

- I have experience in…
- I recently completed…
- My main responsibilities included…
- One of my strengths is…
- I am interested in this role because…
- I am willing to learn new skills.

## 5. Common mistakes

- Giving an answer that is too long.
- Sharing unrelated personal details.
- Claiming skills or experience you do not have.
- Speaking too quickly.
- Memorising a script so rigidly that it sounds unnatural.

## Practice

Write your own introduction in five parts: name, current role or education, experience, relevant strength and reason for applying. Read it aloud and time yourself.

## Learning tip

Be honest and specific. Use one real example to support a strength if the interviewer asks you to explain it.

faq.question: How should I practise this lesson?
faq.answer: Read the examples aloud, practise the dialogue and adapt the phrases to a real situation.

faq.question: Do I need advanced English?
faq.answer: No. Begin with the simple sentences and gradually add detail as your confidence improves.

faq.question: How often should I practise?
faq.answer: A focused 10 to 15 minute practice session most days can help build a useful habit.
